_about: What the wallet page prints: output types and their exposure, the counts of exposed coins by source, the attack models, the proposals, the timelines. Researched by a web agent on 2026-09-23 and edited by hand. Mechanics and public record only; nothing here is advice. CC BY 4.0, Nan · hongdam.net.

outputs.note: The original 2009–2010 output: the public key sits in the open on the chain. Satoshi-era mining rewards are here, about 1.7 million BTC across some 20,000 to 45,000 outputs, untouched since.

outputs.exposed: only when spent, or if the address is reused
outputs.note: The output holds a hash of the key. The key is shown in the spending transaction — so a used address that receives coins again is exposed.

outputs.note: A hash of a script; the script and its keys appear at spend time.

outputs.note: The output is itself a (tweaked) public key, by design, so the key is on the chain from the moment coins arrive. About a third of all outputs by count in 2025, under one percent by value.
Taproot's script tree with the key-path spend removed, so a hash-based or post-quantum script can sit in a leaf. A draft with no activation path.

attacks.name: Long-range
attacks.what: The public key is already on the chain. The attacker can take a month. Every P2PK output, every Taproot output, and every reused address of any type is in this class.

attacks.name: Short-range (on-spend)
attacks.what: The key appears only in the spending transaction, so the attacker must compute the private key and broadcast a competing spend before the honest one is confirmed — about ten minutes, sometimes an hour. Every output type is in this class at the moment of spending.

attacks.name: Harvest now, decrypt later
attacks.what: Does not apply to a wallet. There is no ciphertext to store; a key is either on the chain or it is not.

window.ten_minutes: not possible on atoms — about 10 days per key on 10,000–26,000 atoms
not possible on ions — 25.7 days per key on 19,397 qubits

proposals.name: BIP 360 — P2MR
proposals.who: Hunter Beast, Ethan Heilman, Isabel Foxen Duke
proposals.what: A new output type, SegWit version 2, addresses bc1z: Taproot's script tree without the key path. Renamed twice (P2QRH, P2TSH, P2MR). Status: draft.

proposals.name: BIP 361 — legacy signature sunset
proposals.what: Phase A, about three years after activation: legacy scripts may only send to post-quantum scripts. Phase B, two years later: old signatures no longer verify, with 'rescue' paths for coins provably from a seed phrase. Status: draft.

proposals.name: Hourglass
proposals.what: Rate-limit spends from P2PK outputs to one per block, so a thief could not dump 1.7 million BTC at once.

proposals.name: Commit, delay, reveal
proposals.what: Publish a hash of your transaction first, wait, then reveal it, so an attacker who learns your key at reveal time cannot front-run a transaction committed earlier. Would let exposed keys spend safely after the curve breaks.

proposals.name: Quantum canary
proposals.what: Coins in an address only a quantum machine could open; a spend from it triggers restrictions automatically instead of on a fixed date.

proposals.name: Provable address-control timestamps
proposals.what: Privately timestamp a proof that you control an address now, without moving coins; redeem frozen coins later with a STARK proof.

proposals.name: SHRINCS
proposals.who: Jonas Nick and Mikhail Kudinov, Blockstream
proposals.what: A SHA-256-based signature of about 324 bytes, so post-quantum signatures do not cut throughput to a third of a transaction a second.

proposals.name: Quantum-safe transactions without a fork
proposals.what: Hash-based proofs under today's rules, at $75–$200 of GPU time per transaction; a last resort, its author says.

proposals.name: P2Q
proposals.what: A SegWit version 3 output identical to Taproot, so its key path can be switched off later without touching existing Taproot coins.

elsewhere.what: A roadmap: hash-based validator signatures, signature agility for accounts (EIP-8141, expected in the Hegotá fork), core post-quantum infrastructure around 2029.
First post-quantum transaction on mainnet in November 2025, Falcon-1024 signatures in a stateless contract; consensus itself not yet post-quantum.

timelines.what: 28–49% chance of a 24-hour RSA-2048 break within ten years; 92% of experts give even odds within twenty.
RSA-2048 and 256-bit curves deprecated after 2030, disallowed after 2035 (draft).
'Clearly on the horizon', a few years to a decade or more; blockchains safe today; start preparing now.

no_roadmap.what: Bitcoin has no agreed roadmap, funding or timeline for a post-quantum migration; every proposal above is a draft.
